findingsRaised.finding: J's specBasis citations show the contamination channel is BROADER than the single §4.2 walkthrough A-030 identified. J cited amendment text as the basis for at least five of nine labels, and named the effect itself: F016 'is essentially D-020's own worked example'; F025 'is the literal wrong-policy fixture example named in D-031 as the case a prose-only evaluator would miss and wrongly ALLOW'; F046 'appears purpose-built to test D-029'; F038 turns on D-028's asymmetry note; F049's rationale 'is the exact wording D-019 discusses'. Verified directly against the specification: §5.7.1's own note (line 516) says an evaluator built from §5.7 alone 'omits it, and the wrong-policy fixture then ALLOWs' — a second fixture scenario named WITH its answer.

§5.7.1 (line 523) PUBLISHES ELEVEN OF THE EVALUATOR'S OWN REASON-CODE IDENTIFIERS — EVAL_MANDATE_BINDS_POLICY, EVAL_MANDATE_PRINCIPAL_IS_OWNER and nine others. J cited those identifiers as `specBasis` for F024 and F025. D-031's own recorded caveat rejected making EVAL_CODES normative precisely because it 'welds the specification to the implementation's naming and would make reimplementation a transcription exercise'; the identifiers were published anyway 'for auditability'. A labeller has now used them as the basis for a label, which is the cost that caveat anticipated arriving on the labelling side rather than the reimplementation side.

The harness injected the workspace CLAUDE.md and the user's MEMORY.md before J's first tool call. J quoted the Sentinel entry and noted it revealed 'this work feeds Gate S2' and that gate-signing stays with John. FOURTH labeller to report this channel unprompted (E, G, H, J).
